venues.name: Katz's Delicatessen
venues.address: 205 E Houston St, New York, NY 10002
venues.verdict: The undisputed king of pastrami. Every NYC pastrami conversation starts and ends with Katz's.
venues.whatToOrder: Pastrami on rye with spicy mustard. Tip the carver $2 upfront for thicker slices. Get the half-sour pickles. Skip the fries.

venues.name: 2nd Ave Deli
venues.verdict: The strongest challenger to Katz's throne. Consistently excellent pastrami with a more relaxed dining experience.
venues.whatToOrder: Pastrami sandwich on rye. Add a bowl of matzo ball soup and a Dr. Brown's Cel-Ray. The chopped liver appetizer is also legendary.

venues.name: Pastrami Queen
venues.verdict: The name says it all. Slightly smokier than Katz's, machine-sliced but delicious. The UES pastrami destination.
venues.whatToOrder: Hot pastrami sandwich on rye — ask for extra mustard. Their Romanian pastrami is the signature. Try the knish on the side.

venues.name: Sarge's Delicatessen & Diner
venues.verdict: The best all-around deli in NYC. Maybe not the #1 pastrami, but the best menu and most consistent experience.
venues.whatToOrder: Pastrami sandwich lean or extra-lean on rye. The corned beef is equally excellent. Their combo sandwich (pastrami + corned beef) is the move.

venues.name: David's Brisket House
venues.verdict: Brooklyn's best-kept pastrami secret. Half the price of Manhattan delis with arguably better meat.
venues.whatToOrder: Hot pastrami on a hero roll. The portions are enormous for the price. Their brisket sandwich is equally legendary.

venues.name: Frankel's Delicatessen & Appetizing
venues.verdict: The modern deli renaissance leader. Hand-carved pastrami that rivals Katz's in a hip Greenpoint setting.
venues.whatToOrder: The pastrami breakfast sandwich was called 'the greatest breakfast sandwich' by the New York Times. Their hand-carved pastrami on rye is also excellent.

venues.name: S&P Lunch
venues.verdict: Formerly Eisenberg's Sandwich Shop (est. 1929), rebranded but still serving exceptional old-school pastrami.
venues.whatToOrder: Hot pastrami on rye. The old-school lunch counter vibe makes everything taste better. Grab a chocolate egg cream to wash it down.

venues.name: Liebman's Deli
venues.verdict: The Bronx's last great kosher deli. They brine their own pastrami in-house — the real deal.
venues.whatToOrder: Pastrami on rye — they brine it themselves. The potato pancakes and matzo ball soup are must-try sides.

venues.name: Hometown Bar-B-Que
venues.verdict: Not a deli, but their smoked pastrami is one of the best versions in the city — BBQ meets Jewish deli tradition.
venues.whatToOrder: The smoked pastrami plate with sides. If they have the pastrami-spiced lamb belly, get that too. Arrive early on weekends — they sell out.

venues.name: Carnegie Deli at Madison Square Garden
venues.verdict: The legendary Carnegie Deli lives on inside Madison Square Garden. Same towering sandwiches, limited access.
venues.whatToOrder: The massive pastrami sandwich — Carnegie was always famous for piling it impossibly high. Same spirit lives on at MSG.

venues.name: Ben's Kosher Deli
venues.verdict: Queens' kosher deli institution. A true neighborhood joint that delivers solid, old-school pastrami.
venues.whatToOrder: Pastrami on rye with mustard. Their combo platter with pastrami, corned beef, and coleslaw is a crowd favorite.
